# pydoccraft

> Python document extraction, rendering, conversion and authoring using in-process Rust engines. The import name is `doc_ex`. The documentation describes the development branch; check releases for availability.

## Documentation

- [Python API](https://narain1.github.io/pydoccraft/docs/api.html): opening documents, extracting pages, models, rendering and conversion.
- [Formats and fidelity](https://narain1.github.io/pydoccraft/docs/formats.html): supported formats, conversions and known limitations.
- [Cookbook](https://narain1.github.io/pydoccraft/docs/cookbook.html): practical authoring workflows.
- [Authoring](https://narain1.github.io/pydoccraft/docs/authoring.html): creating and editing documents.
- [Markdown and assets](https://narain1.github.io/pydoccraft/docs/markdown-assets.html): exporting Markdown and referenced media.
- [Safety](https://narain1.github.io/pydoccraft/docs/safety.html): input limits and error handling.
- [Operation support matrix](https://narain1.github.io/pydoccraft/docs/support-matrix.html): operation-level support and evidence.
- [Repository](https://github.com/narain1/pydoccraft): source, issues and release information.

## Quick example

```python
from pathlib import Path
import doc_ex

with doc_ex.open("report.pdf") as document:
    print(document[0].get_text())
    Path("page.png").write_bytes(document[0].get_pixmap(dpi=144))
```

Pages are zero-indexed. HTML extraction via `page.get_text("html")` is unreleased and returns semantic content, not a layout reproduction. EPUB support is also unreleased; EPUB chapters are not physical pages and PNG rendering is unavailable. Conversion is not pixel-perfect. No runtime downloads, external executables, cloud credentials or OCR are required.
